root_cause: The tab navigation keyboard handler (_keydown) uses getNextActiveElement without checking for disabled tabs, so ArrowRight/ArrowLeft can move focus onto a disabled tab which cannot be activated.
repair_strategy: Modify _keydown in tab.js to iterate getNextActiveElement until an enabled (non-disabled) tab is found, using the imported isDisabled utility.
expected_accessibility_effect: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft keyboard navigation will skip disabled tabs, moving focus to the next enabled tab and activating its associated panel, conforming to ARIA authoring practices for tablist navigation.
functional_risks: If all tabs are disabled, the loop could become infinite (though this scenario is unlikely).
Custom implementations that depend on landing on disabled tabs for other behavior may be affected.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowRight on the first tab moves focus to and activates the third tab (billing) when the middle tab is disabled.
Verify that ArrowLeft from the last tab wraps to the first enabled tab.
Ensure disabled tabs remain unfocusable and retain aria-selected=false.
Confirm that mouse clicks and programmatic tab activation continue to work as before.
